1	# Rules: Project Landing Page
2	
3	- **R-v7q.** A project's Needs you lists the same things Home does, for that project alone, newest first, and isn't shown when nothing needs the person there.
4	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
5	- **R-2hx.** A design with a branch is listed under In progress and not under Designs; once its branch is finished, it's listed under Designs again.
6	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
7	- **R-k4n.** Pushing a branch is always asked first, saying which branch goes to which remote, and nothing is pushed until the person says yes.
8	  *shown-on: /f/:project/branches/:branch/publish @ typical*
9	- **R-8dz.** The page's work and its app follow what happens elsewhere without a reload: a turn, a build, a push or a merge changes them as it happens, and they're read again every five minutes for what Prelude can't see, such as a pull request merged on the Git server.
10	- **R-wm3.** New design offers the design system and the app shell as kinds only until the project has one of each.
11	  *shown-on: /f/:project/designs/new @ new-project*
12	- **R-r6b.** A design under Designs says it's ready to build when it has approved pages not yet built, and only once the project's app exists. A design that changed since it was approved isn't ready: it says it changed, until it's approved again.
13	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
14	- **R-h2w.** Once the app is built, it can be run from the project's own folder with a command and address of its own, never the design host's, and the Run button always shows the command it runs, so clicking it is the approval.
15	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
16	- **R-p7c.** Building or connecting the app sets how it runs from here, so a newly built app can be run without setting anything; a command changed on this page applies on this computer only.
17	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
18	- **R-5tj.** The app run from here opens in the browser once it answers at its address, and stops when Prelude quits.
19	- *

1	# Project Landing Page - notes
2	
3	A project's own page (`/f/<id>`), a redesign of `server/views/_folder.eta` (with
4	`_branch.eta`), whose model is built in `server/main.js` (`view()` in the
5	`/f/:id` handler). Home (prelude/landing-page) gathers what needs the person
6	across projects and links here; this page holds the project's whole picture.
7	
8	Pages: `/f/:project` (Project), `/f/:project/designs/new` (New design, modal),
9	`/f/:project/branches/:branch/publish` (Push a branch, modal),
10	`/f/:project/cleanup` (Clean up, modal). Fragments:
11	`/f/:project/work`, `/f/:project/app`. States: typical (spark-lending), new
12	project, app being built, update clashed (with the app on the shell's branch
13	and a failed push), long names (an existing app to connect, no remote),
14	large project (a hundred features).
15	
16	## Decisions (the person asked for all eleven, 2026-10-18)
17	
18	1. **On the design system**, not ds/v1 + `prelude.css`, like Home.
19	2. **Work beside setup**: a `.split` in a `.center.wide`. Main: Needs you, In
20	   progress, Designs. Side: The app, What the agent can read. Added
21	   `.center.wide` / `--measure-wide` to the design system (46rem can't hold a
22	   split).
23	3. **New design is a modal**, opened by the header's "New design…", the page's
24	   one primary action. A refused title comes back into the fields alone
25	   (`_new-design-fields`); made, the modal closes and the page refreshes (the
26	   real app opens the new design's page).
27	4. **One primary per view**: Merge, Push, Start the app build are plain buttons.
28	5. **A branch's state as pills**: check, building / build stopped, behind main,
29	   pull request open, nothing done yet. Stories get a state pill (Built, To
30	   build, Building) and "A change". "Also changes" is a disclosure with the

1	# A merged pull request shows as merged
2	
3	For anyone who finishes designs by pushing them for a pull request. Today a pushed branch says "Pull request open" forever, even after its pull request was merged. That's worse after a squash merge, or when someone keeps working on the branch after the merge. Those branches also never leave In progress, so the list fills with work that's already done. Once this is built, a branch says its pull request was merged as soon as what was pushed is in main. A branch with nothing left over goes away by itself. A branch with work left over says how much, so the person knows whether anything still needs pushing.
4	
5	## What changes
6	
7	- A pushed branch shows "Pull request open" only until what was pushed is in main. This holds however it was merged: a merge commit, a rebase or a squash.
8	- Once the pull request is merged, a branch with nothing new on it is tidied up by itself, as a branch merged here already is. It leaves In progress, and its design is listed under Designs again.
9	- A branch with commits made after it was pushed stays under In progress. Instead of "Pull request open", it shows "Pull request merged" and a warning, e.g. "2 commits since".
10	- Under it, a line says when its pull request was merged into main. It also says that the commits made since aren't in main, and that they can be pushed for another pull request.
11	- That branch no longer offers "Open the pull request". It offers "Push and open a pull request…" again.
12	
13	## Acceptance criteria
14	
15	- **R-t5w.** A branch's pull request shows as open only until what was pushed is in main, however it was merged, squashed included; a branch whose work is all in main is tidied up by itself, and one with commits since says how many.
16	- A pushed branch whose pull request hasn't been merged still shows "Pull request open" and "Open the pull request".
17	- A branch whose pull request was squash-merged on the Git server, with nothing committed since, leaves

1	# Clean up what Prelude leaves behind
2	
3	For anyone who has worked on a project for a while and finds old branches and worktree folders piling up. Prelude tidies a branch by itself only when all its work is in main. Everything else stays: a branch with commits after its pull request merged, a branch it lost track of, one made and never used, a folder left behind, and the copies on the remote. Today the person has to find these by hand in git. Once this is built, the project page lists them in one place, with why each is there. Only the ones that are safe to remove start picked, and nothing goes until the person says so.
4	
5	## What changes
6	
7	- When Prelude has found anything it won't tidy by itself, In progress's heading has a "Clean up…" button showing how many. With nothing in progress, a line of its own says how many branches and folders there are, with the same button.
8	- Clean up opens in a dialog over the page, titled "Clean up" and the project's name. It explains that Prelude removes a branch by itself once its work is in main, and that these are what it leaves to the person.
9	- Under "On this computer", each branch or folder shows:
10	  - its name, and what it is: "Pull request merged", "In main", "Nothing done on it", "Not in Prelude's list" or "Folder only"
11	  - warnings where work would be lost: "2 commits since", "1 commit not in main", "2 files not committed"
12	  - a sentence saying why it's there, e.g. "Made for Closing day checklist 2 weeks ago, and never worked on."
13	  - for a merged pull request with commits since, which files changed since
14	  - its folder, or that it's a branch with no worktree
15	- Only those whose work is all in main, or with nothing done, start picked. The person can pick or unpick any of them.
16	- A branch the agent is working in shows "Working" and can't be picked until its turn ends.
17	- Branches on the remote are listed apart, under "On origin". A warning says others can see them, and to pick one only if n

**Views** (`server/views/projects/`)
- `_work.eta` and `_branch.eta` are ported over the app's, element for element: the Clean up… button with its count (or a line of its own when nothing is in progress), and the merged pull request's pills and line.
- `_cleanup.eta` (the modal) and `_cleaned.eta` (the notice) are new.
- `page.eta` is unchanged: the design's page was already identical to the app's, and only its partials changed. No styles changed.
- In routes.json every view, form and answer now points at `@app/server/views/projects/…`, and the two `"from"` entries are gone.

**Git side** (`server/branches.js`)
- **Whether work is in main** (`isIn`): Prelude now tries the merge without making it (`git merge-tree --write-tree`). If merging would change nothing, the work counts as in main. So a squash-merged or rebased branch is tidied up by itself (R-t5w).
- **The pull request** (`pullRequest()`): a push now records which commit was pushed. The pull request counts as merged once that commit is in main, and `since` counts the commits made after it. Home's "pull request open" uses the same test. After each fetch, a pull request whose state changed tells the page to reload, so a merge on the Git server shows up without waiting for the five-minute read.
- **What Clean up finds** (`leftBehind()`), read from git and Prelude's own list of worktrees only:
  - branches whose pull request merged with commits since;
  - branches never worked on, once they're a week old;
  - `prelude/` branches Prelude no longer lists;
  - leftover folders in its worktrees;
  - `origin/prelude/` branches whose work is in main.
- **Removing** (`clear()`) takes only what was picked, checked against a fresh read, so the form can't name anything else. A branch the agent is working in is refused even if it was posted (R-m2e). Any design host running in a worktree is stopped first.

**Model and handlers**
- `server/project.js`: types for `pullRequest` and `cleanup` that fit all six states, and the code that fills them.
- `server/main.js`: `GET`/`POST /f/:id/cleanup`, answering as routes.json says (the modal closes, the page reloads in `workspace`, the notice says what went). The cleanup URL is added to the app layout's paths, and fetches now prune, so branches already deleted on the server aren't offered.

**RULES.md:** I removed the *proposed* line from R-t5w, R-c3j, R-9xk and R-m2e. R-m2e counts as touched because Clean up is where both of its halves apply. NOTES.md has a new "Built" section; the stories and the design agree.

**Worth looking at before approving the screens and opening the pull request:**
- **Clean up deletes things.** On origin it runs `git push origin --delete`. Try it on a throwaway repository first.
- **Where it differs from the design** (all in NOTES.md):
  - "Merged 3 days ago" is when Prelude first saw the work in main, not when the server merged it.
  - `gh`/`az` don't confirm a pull request's state, because they'd run on every read of the page.
  - If main edits the same lines again after a squash merge, the test reads that branch as not in main. It stays In progress with its pull request "open".
  - A removal that fails is only logged and the item stays listed: the notice has no place to say why.
- **Needs git 2.38 or later** for `merge-tree --write-tree`. On older git it falls back to the old ancestry test, so squash-merged branches stay until removed by hand.
